## Review-round 1 continuation handoff — Chapter 1B only

Filesystem writes were unavailable, so `research-materials.md` and `research-ledger-manifest.json` were not modified. The entries below are append-ready and continue after `E033`; no scores were assigned.

### New accepted evidence units

| ID | Source and precise locator | Claim and evidentiary role | Lens mapping |
|---|---|---|---|
| E034 | [P5 Joint Statement](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zzjg_663340/xos_664404/xwlb_664406/202201/t20220103_10478505.html), Chinese MFA, 3 Jan 2022, HTML ¶¶64–70 | China joined a commitment that nuclear war cannot be won, that states should prevent unauthorized or unintended use, avoid arms races, and pursue dialogue. High confidence for the diplomatic act; implementation remains unverified. | 1B.2, 1B.3, 1B.4, 1B.8 |
| E035 | [China NPT disarmament statement](https://un.china-mission.gov.cn/eng/chinaandun/disarmament_armscontrol/npt/202208/t20220810_10738603.htm), Chinese UN Mission, 5 Aug 2022, HTML ¶¶37–51 | China reaffirmed NFU, minimum capability, avoidance of accidental or unauthorized launch, strategic-stability dialogue involving cyber and AI, CTBT support, and fissile-material negotiations. Formal policy evidence, not proof of implementation. | 1B.2, 1B.3, 1B.4, 1B.7, 1B.8, 1B.9, 1B.10 |
| E036 | [Peaceful nuclear uses statement](https://un.china-mission.gov.cn/eng/chinaandun/disarmament_armscontrol/npt/202208/t20220810_10738711.htm), Chinese UN Mission, 8 Aug 2022, HTML ¶¶31–39, 48–54 | China described safeguards, nuclear-security cooperation, IAEA engagement, nuclear-facility security, and HEU-to-LEU conversion cooperation. Official self-report; useful for mechanisms and commitments, weak for independent effectiveness. | 1B.3, 1B.4, 1B.7, 1B.9 |
| E037 | [Fu Cong NPT statement](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zzjg_663340/jks_665232/jkxw_665234/202208/t20220803_10732780.html), Chinese MFA, 2 Aug 2022, HTML ¶¶79–99 | China linked nuclear policy to NPT obligations, NFU, minimum capability, JCPOA implementation, Korean Peninsula denuclearization, and nuclear-risk dialogue. Distinct from E035 because it adds regional nonproliferation and JCPOA positions. | 1B.2, 1B.4, 1B.6, 1B.8, 1B.9 |
| E038 | [MFA response to U.S. arsenal estimate](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/xw/fyrbt/lxjzh/202405/t20240530_11347415.html), Chinese MFA, 30 Nov 2022, HTML ¶¶61–72 | China publicly characterized its nuclear policy as defensive, NFU-based, restrained, and limited to minimum requirements. This is a self-presentational rebuttal, not independent confirmation. | 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.7, 1B.10 |
| E039 | [Unknowns About China’s Nuclear Modernization](https://www.armscontrol.org/act/2023-06/features/unknowns-about-chinas-nuclear-modernization-program), Arms Control Association, June 2023, HTML ¶¶91–105, 153–161 | Specialist retrospective analysis reports continued NFU reaffirmation, centralized civilian control, low peacetime readiness, modernization since roughly 2019, and that Xi would have to approve major nuclear-force changes. It establishes attribution capacity, not a documented 2022 command decision. | 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.3, 1B.7, 1B.8, 1B.10 |
| E040 | [China Position Paper on Responsible Military Use of AI](https://us.china-embassy.gov.cn/eng/zgyw/202201/t20220113_10492264.htm), Chinese Embassy/MFA, 12 Jan 2022, HTML ¶¶15–30 | China called for human control, accountability, international rules, and safeguards against harmful or uncontrolled military AI use. Strong evidence of declared governance position; no implementation audit located. | 1B.9 |
| E041 | [China’s Nuclear Signaling and the Ukraine War](https://cms.apln.network/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/PB-88-Tong-Zhao.pdf), APLN/Tong Zhao, Oct 2022, PDF pp.2–5 | Expert analysis argues China could learn coercive signaling from Russia while retaining formal NFU, especially in a Taiwan contingency. This is contrary-risk analysis, not evidence that Xi adopted such a policy. | 1B.2, 1B.5, 1B.8, 1B.10 |
| E042 | [China suspends military and other cooperation with the U.S.](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/beijing-halts-highlevel-military-dialogue-with-us-suspends-other-cooperation-2864888), Reuters, 5 Aug 2022, article ¶¶418–424 | After Pelosi’s Taiwan visit, Beijing suspended senior military dialogue and a maritime-security mechanism while conducting unprecedented exercises around Taiwan. Direct target-year crisis evidence; attribution is to Beijing, not necessarily a personal Xi order. | 1B.5, 1B.8 |
| E043 | [China warns further Taiwan activity would destabilize relations](https://www.axios.com/2022/08/16/china-ambassador-warns-taiwan-response-us), Axios, 16 Aug 2022, article ¶¶45–54 | Chinese ambassador linked further U.S. activity to renewed tensions and inability to conduct nuclear-security dialogue; reporting also records drills and competing U.S. claims of coercion. Mixed evidence of crisis communication failure and escalation risk. | 1B.5, 1B.8 |
| E044 | [Engaging China on Strategic Stability and Mutual Vulnerability](https://carnegieendowment.org/research/2022/10/engaging-china-on-strategic-stability-and-mutual-vulnerability?lang=en), Carnegie Endowment, Oct 2022, HTML ¶¶106–139, 230–247 | Expert analysis identifies failed U.S.–China strategic dialogue, nuclear/conventional/cyber C2 entanglement, misperception risks, and the need for crisis-management measures. It does not establish Xi-specific misconduct. | 1B.3, 1B.5, 1B.8, 1B.9, 1B.10 |
| E045 | [China’s response to the U.S. Nuclear Posture Review](https://un.china-mission.gov.cn/eng/chinaandun/disarmament_armscontrol/unga/202210/t20221029_10793966.htm), Chinese UN Mission, 28 Oct 2022, HTML ¶¶31–41 | China again stated NFU, minimum capability, no arms race, and opposition to threats against nonnuclear states. Official reaffirmation; no independent verification of implementation. | 1B.2, 1B.4, 1B.8, 1B.10 |
| E046 | [Nuclear Safety Law of the PRC](https://www.caea.gov.cn/n6760401/n6760402/c6827752/content.html), China Atomic Energy Authority, republished 23 Apr 2022, HTML ¶¶42–46, 68–70, 93–137, 145–160 | The law establishes prevention, independent regulation, responsibility allocation, physical protection, emergency capacity, information rights, and international cooperation. It was enacted in 2017, so this is an inherited legal mechanism rather than a new Xi-period reform. | 1B.3, 1B.4, 1B.9 |
| E047 | [BWC statement by Zhao Lijian](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/mfa_eng/xw/fyrbt/lxjzh/202405/t20240530_11347260.html), Chinese MFA, 11 Apr 2022, HTML ¶¶74–82 | China called biological weapons an absolute red line, supported BWC verification, reported commitment to obligations, and cited the Tianjin Biosecurity Guidelines. Official policy evidence; implementation and transparency remain unresolved. | 1B.6, 1B.9 |
| E048 | [Xi Jinping’s 20th Party Congress report](https://app.www.gov.cn/govdata/gov/202210/25/493662/article.html), State Council portal, Oct 2022, HTML ¶¶188–205 | The report called for centralized national-security leadership, nuclear/cyber/biological risk systems, early-warning and emergency coordination, stronger strategic deterrence, and optimized joint command. This is the clearest target-period attribution baseline for policy direction and command authority, but not proof of realized safety outcomes. | 1B.3, 1B.6, 1B.7, 1B.9, 1B.10 |

### Candidate outcomes and saturation

- The NNSA 2022 annual-report index was opened as a source-family lead, but the underlying PDF failed retrieval; it remains gateway-only and was not counted.
- The Chinese-language BWC statement was found, but the English MFA press-conference record provided the accessible precise locator and was retained as E047.
- No public 2022 record was found documenting a Xi-directed nuclear command-and-control reform, launch-safety incident, arms-control implementation milestone, or independent audit of NFU credibility.
- No independently verified target-year evidence was found linking Xi personally to cyber, biological, or AI-risk implementation beyond formal policy and organizational direction.
- The chapter is provisionally saturated for this continuation: further search is likely to yield repeated official policy statements or capability estimates rather than new independent attribution evidence.

### Deduplication and attribution controls

- E034, E035, E037, E038, and E045 are separate claim units but concentrated in the same Chinese official source family; they must not count as independent corroboration of implementation.
- E001/E002 remain overlapping arsenal-expansion estimates and should not be treated as two fully independent force-growth confirmations.
- E039, E041, and E044 provide independent specialist interpretation but do not prove Xi personally ordered escalation or abandoned NFU.
- E042/E043 document Beijing-level crisis conduct and communication breakdown; neither establishes a personal command order or nuclear threat.
- E046 is inherited legal infrastructure, not evidence of a new 2022 reform.
- Formal commitments, capability estimates, and institutional authority are now clearly separated from implementation, sincerity, and personal responsibility.

### Local-data audit

- `LF001` and `LF005`: retained as inherited nuclear exposure and stockpile context only.
- `LF002`: not reused because it duplicates the supplied total-inventory context.
- `LF003`: missing-value observation; retained only as an upstream data-quality gap, not evidence.
- `LF004`: operational strategic-warhead context, but not sufficient for attribution; not reused in this continuation.

No score, range, anchor, ranking, or judge recommendation was produced.
